claim: On the same 543 benchmark bond observations, quantum beats learned by only 0.3129 kcal/mol of mean |error| (paired t p=5.37e-05) while Wilcoxon (p=0.553) and the sign test (246 quantum-better vs 284 learned-better, p=0.108) are null; quantum vs reference is an unambiguous 3.3882 kcal/mol gap with both tests at p<1e-50.
value_found: q-vs-l: mean(ae_q-ae_l)=-0.31289 (MAE 2.09781 vs 2.41070), median diff=+0.0200, paired t=-4.07128 p=5.3725e-05, Wilcoxon W=68265 p=0.553016 (two independent implementations agree), sign 246/284 with 13 ties p=0.107928. q-vs-r: mean=-3.38816 (MAE 5.48597), median=-3.4100, t=-19.2489 p=2.616e-63, Wilcoxon W=14376.5 p=1.921e-59, sign 451/92/0 ties p=7.822e-58. All match the claim.
unit: bond observation (one row = one independent paired comparison); 543 rows = 543 unique observation_ids = 543 unique (molecule, fragment_a, fragment_b) triples, 419 unique parent molecules, 539 unique fragment pairs; errors = |channel_estimate - experimental| per row, differenced within row (fully paired).
method: python3 /data/user/conversations/conv-75e3fc1d-c4c9-41b5-800b-05f4632eec99/project/output/analysis/verify_4_paired.py (independent script over data/normalized_views/experimental_benchmark.tsv; no import of workstream code); stats.ttest_rel/ttest_1samp, scipy.stats.wilcoxon plus a hand-written tie-corrected normal-approximation Wilcoxon, exact binomial sign test, vectorised molecule-cluster sign-flip permutation (100k reps).
notes: Every number in the claim reproduces to the stated precision from the raw TSV (and the TSV is bit-identical to the source workbook on all four value columns: 543/543 keys, max abs diff 0.0). No evidence was found for any of the standard refutation routes: (1) the sign-test count is not sensitive to the tie convention (all 13 ties are exactly 0.000 |err| differences; excluding them gives 246/284, p=0.10793 with or without ties); (2) the Wilcoxon null is not a scipy artefact - a hand-implemented tie-corrected signed-rank test gives the identical W=68265 and p=0.553016, and pratt/zsplit conventions give p=0.614, i.e. even more null, so the claimed 0.553 is the most favourable non-exact convention; (3) the t/Wilcoxon divergence is a genuine scale-vs-rank effect, not a data error: the sign of the mean is carried by a few large |err| differences (dropping the 10 largest leaves mean -0.139, p=0.0094, Wilcoxon p=0.876) while the median is exactly +0.020 with 284/246 splitting the other way - both the t p=5.37e-05 and the Wilcoxon p=0.553 are individually correct statements about different features of the same difference vector. Caveat the claim does not state: the 543 rows are heterogeneous literature values, not independent repeats (per data_manifest warning), and 124 rows share a parent molecule with another row; a molecule-cluster sign-flip permutation of the mean gives p=4e-05 (q-vs-l) and p=1e-05 (q-vs-r) rather than the nominal t p-values, so the t p-value is mildly anti-conservative but the ordering is unchanged and the q-vs-r conclusion is robust to dropping up to 10 largest outliers and to cluster resampling (q-vs-r cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [-3.872,-3.087]). The q-vs-r 'both tests at p<1e-50' statement checks out (t p=2.6e-63, Wilcoxon p=1.9e-59). Separately, the ~165 number seen in output/results/ws5_heterogeneity.json ('pooled_within_sd'=165.2622713320976 for within-molecule experimental spread) IS a formula error, but it belongs to a different analysis (not claim 4): the original ws5_het.py computes sqrt(sum(w_i * var_i^2)/sum(w_i)) - it squares each per-group variance a second time before pooling, so the estimator has kcal^4 units and is not an SD. The correct df-weighted pooled within-molecule SD is 9.9654 kcal/mol (equivalent naive variance-weighted form sqrt(sum(w_i*var_i)/sum(w_i)) also gives 9.9654, so pooling form is not the issue); the companion 'mean_within_sd'=106.4101 is likewise mislabeled - it is var.mean() in kcal^2, not an SD. Any report sentence quoting 165 kcal/mol as an experimental noise scale should be corrected to 9.97 kcal/mol.
